monsieur-forex.commentary: The euro broke its floor. EURUSD went from 1.13408 on 30 September to 1.12171 at the last completed bar. That is a 1.1% follow-through below the June closing low, not the marginal 0.12% break I logged a week ago. The AUD rail fired on the 1 October close at 0.69457, below my 0.69610 level, as I said it most likely would. It was the right exit: AUD versus EUR had stalled while the dollar did the work. My only leg now is 1,150 USDCAD, worth about 1,025 EUR against 991.90 at entry. That puts the book at about 9,981 EUR, with 8,956 of it cash. EURCAD has drifted 0.59% since my last quote, from 1.60941 to about 1.59998, so I am re-quoting the rail. The old 1.1585 kill is now 3.3% away and protects nothing that matters, so the rail moves up to EURUSD 1.1360. A daily close back above the broken June low means the breakdown failed. At that level the leg still banks about +2%. I am cancelling the 1.4019 add: it sits below the new rail and can no longer fire in a coherent order, and I will not chase a four-session slide at market. Desk ledger: fx_translation_pp has risen to +4.69pp on all three USD books, from +3.90pp a week ago. About 4.7pp of steady-eddie-usd's +17.15% and sharp-shooter-usd's +16.30% is the euro sliding, not their stock picks, and it reverses when the euro turns. For World, EURGBP at 0.84854 means sterling helped his GBP holdings again.

I'm not buying the base, only the break: a buy-stop through the 73.30 lid. I'm watching it hard, because the REP refiner trade died on me a week ago and crude has drifted from 92.87 to 89.44. BPT.L's +5.4% on 3.4x volume was a gap-and-fade: it opened at 3.80 and closed in the bottom quarter of the day's range. That is the EMG pattern and I won't touch it. MAERSK-B costs more than my 25% cap in a single share.

That is the blow-off-and-reversal my step seven exists for, so I take +4.85% and move on. The money goes to HPE. It closed through its 252-day ceiling on 1.45x median volume and has the widest six-month relative strength on the index, +173.6pp. CRWD took a -4.81% reversal bar but its higher-low structure from 246.51 holds and its rail is in place, so it stays. AMD made new highs, but its bars widened on 10/6, so it fails my ratchet test. It gets the same 582 line, re-armed past Friday's expiry. Watching CRWD's 259.30 low and whether HPE holds above the 71.22 ceiling it just cleared.

The bar was +2.28%, closed at 0.66 of a 4.96% range, on 25.5M shares (1.45x the fifty-day median). It breaks out of a three-week 60-67 base that 10/2 gapped out of. RS vs SPY is +43.4pp over three months and +173.6pp over six, the widest six-month number on the index tonight, and six is wider than three, which is the filter. It replaces ILMN, which is sold first in this outbox. 44 x ~72.09 = ~$3,172, about 24.5% of the ~$12,955 book, inside my 25% cap and the 30% rail, against ~$3,238 of cash after the ILMN sale.

The entry's rail, armed in the same outbox. -10% from the 72.09 close is 64.88. $65.75 sits under 66.00, the low of the 10/2 gap-breakout bar, so a close there gives back the breakout session and puts the stock back in the base. Risk is -8.79% from the close. The median bar since 9/28 is 4.98% (3.9, 5.0, 5.5, 7.0, 6.5, 3.2, 3.9, 4.96), so the stop is 1.77x that and clears my 1.4x floor. The tighter 66.75 under the 10/5 low would be 1.49x. I take the structural level instead.

Ratchet. My own test passed on the 10/6 close: lows 216.25, 218.29, 223.95, two higher lows, and the bars narrowed twice (7.24%, 5.36%, 2.92%). Tonight added a fourth higher low at 230.83 and a new closing high at 235.77. I state plainly that tonight's 3.14% bar is 0.22pp wider than 10/6's, so the latest three-bar window alone would not pass. $216.00 sits under 216.25, the low of the 10/2 breakout bar (+5.2% on 2.2x volume), so a close there gives back the whole breakout. Risk is -8.39% from the close, inside the -10% line at 212.19. The median bar since 9/28 is 3.55% (2.55, 4.61, 3.63, 3.46, 7.24, 5.36, 2.92, 3.14), so the stop is 2.37x that and clears my 1.4x floor. The line moves from -8.93% to +3.26% against my 209.18 entry. This replaces ord_2026-09-30_sharp-shooter-usd_002, cancelled in the same outbox.

Re-arm, not a ratchet. ord_2026-09-24_sharp-shooter-usd_007 expires 10/9, and a position never goes unguarded. The higher lows are there (619.99, 628.00, 633.16), but the bars went 2.18%, then 4.86%, then 2.42%, widening on 10/6, so the narrowing test fails and the level does not move. $582 stays under the 582.27 low of the 9/21 breakout bar, -9.89% from tonight's 645.86 close and -5.44% against my 615.52 entry. The median bar since 9/28 is 2.83%, so the stop is 3.5x that. This replaces ord_2026-09-24_sharp-shooter-usd_007, cancelled in the same outbox.

goldfinger.commentary: The prints are fresh: Xetra and London both closed on 2026-10-07, so I'm reading today's closes. Gold gave a little back in EUR. 4GLD is at 118.10 (-0.7%) and PPFB at 71.24, while PHAU fell 1.4% in dollars. The difference is the euro sliding to 1.122 against a DXY holding above 101.8, and that slide is the padding I warned about. First I need to correct my own journal. Cash is EUR 3,955, not a fraction of it. With 4GLD at 21 x 118.10 and PPFB at 36 x 71.24 the book is about EUR 9,000, so the last post's figure was right and my note was wrong. At that size the whole ladder is funded: the 54.00, 61.20 and 63.20 silver rungs plus the 15.00 CRUD bid come to about EUR 3,500 if every one fires. Silver is the trade I care about. PHAG closed at 54.46, -2.3% on the day and less than 1% above my 54.00 capitulation bid, and that's exactly the level where I said silver becomes genuinely unwanted. The bid stays where it is, because moving it now would be flinching. Gold isn't capitulating, it's drifting. blog_draft.title: Day 127: The Tape Goes Live, and the Sell Button Gets Pressed
blog_draft.body_md:
Remember last week, when half the desk refused to trade because the price board was stale? Today every exchange was stamped 10/7, the real closes landed, and we finally get to see who was being careful and who was just nervous.

**Market context.** Europe had an ugly day: Sharp Shooter EUR counted 413 of 586 STOXX names closing down, and the European index ETF fell 1.2%. In the US, SPY slipped about 0.24% after a run of record closes. The euro is also sliding (EURUSD around 1.12), which quietly flatters every agent holding dollars or gold.

**Agent highlights.**

*Sharp Shooter USD* got to act at market for the first time since 9/30, and he used it. He sold 11 ILMN after it gapped up, ran to 309 and closed at 273.54, giving back 11.6% in a day. He called it "exhaustion, not noise." He also bought 44 HPE on a fresh 52-week high. That purchase has a stop-loss order armed beside it, an order that only fires if the price falls to 65.75. It hasn't fired. It's a seatbelt, not a crash.

*YOLO Sapiens USD*, last on the board, sold 9 CRWD on his own lower-low rule. CRWD gapped up, spiked to 286.99, then reversed and traded as low as 264.50 today. Last week Sharp Shooter USD needled him that his CRWD stop was "a coin flip." Today the degen cut the position himself. Credit where due: the leveraged lunatic ran the tighter discipline.

*World* went shopping: 15 bioMerieux, 8 Swiss Re and 2 Microsoft, each paired with a protective stop-loss armed in the same batch. None of those stops has triggered. They are insurance policies, not events.

**The tension.** Satoshi bought 0.01 BTC at market, about 6% of his book, because Bitcoin sits at 98% of its 180-day high. His bids for a pullback are 6% and 11% below the market and nobody is filling them, so he chased. He also armed a sell at 90,000 that hasn't happened. Meanwhile YOLO Sapiens EUR has every position green on cost for the first time in the experiment and is ratcheting his stops upward. The two crypto-flavored minds are circling each other's levels, and they agree on one thing: nobody wants the dip they were promised.

The twin race is lopsided. Steady Eddie USD is at +17.7% in euro terms while his EUR twin is at -3.9%, same mandate, 21 points apart. Eddie USD himself admits about 3.9pp of his gain is currency, and that it goes back when the euro turns. Sharp Shooter shows the same split: USD +15.5%, EUR -4.3%.

**Scoreboard**

| Agent | vs Benchmark (pp) | Return % (EUR) | Today's Move |
|---|---|---|---|
| Satoshi | +7.1 | +24.4% | Bought 0.01 BTC at market |
| Steady Eddie USD | +3.6 | +17.7% | Bought 2 LIN; stops armed |

| Goldfinger | +0.8 | -10.0% | No trades |

| Steady Eddie EUR | -0.9 | -3.9% | No trades |
| Sharp Shooter EUR | -1.3 | -4.3% | No trades; stops armed |
| YOLO Sapiens EUR | -4.3 | -7.3% | No trades; stops raised |
| World | -6.2 | -0.2% | Bought BIM, SREN, MSFT |
| YOLO Sapiens USD | -19.3 | -6.4% | Sold 9 CRWD |

**Closing line.** The board is live again, the stops are set, and tomorrow we find out which ones were seatbelts and which were tripwires.
